notes:
First Early Testing release of the new Pacto Tech software platform.

The Pacto Tech Utility for Windows: live controller status and input testing, full remapping for XInput and keyboard outputs, mode controls with editable shortcuts, customizable on-screen overlays and themes, kiosk/lockdown modes for cabinets, ready-made scripts for LaunchBox and other frontends, and automatic app updates on your chosen channel.

New firmware for every current board (1000T, 2000T, 2000H, 3000T, 4000T, 4000H, 4000H2, SNAP2, SNAP4 - including the F103VB chip variants of the 2000H/4000H and the F103ZE-based 4000H2) introduces in-app firmware updates: flash your board once with the matching ST-Link image from this release, and every update after that installs from inside the Utility with a couple of clicks. Updates are checked against your exact board model AND its chip, an interrupted update can't brick the board, and a file for the wrong board simply won't apply. Boards with the smaller F103VB chip keep updating via ST-Link (no room for the update system on that chip) - the Utility tells you when a new version is out for them.

Also improved: much cleaner switching between arcade (XInput) and gamepad/keyboard (DISS.) modes, per-input mode settings, twin-stick 1P/2P modes, and turbo refinements.

The Utility can now flash boards with an ST-Link, right from the app.

If your board is on firmware from before in-app updates existed (or has the F103VB chip), you no longer need any external flashing tools: connect an ST-Link V2 to the board's SWD header, pick your board model in the Utility's firmware section, and press Flash. The app reads the chip itself, downloads the matching signed image, and refuses anything that doesn't fit your exact hardware.

Also fixes update-signature verification for in-app firmware updates.

Fixes from early testing feedback.

Flashing with ST-Link is more resilient: if the chip can't be reached, the Utility keeps retrying with clear guidance - check the wiring, make sure the board has its own power, and power-cycle it. Detect once, then flash - no extra tools needed.

Test screen voice announcements now stop when the Utility window is in the background or closed to the tray.

Update checks and downloads no longer hang - a failed firmware download says so clearly and can be retried. The What's-new list now explains when releases exist on a different update channel than yours, and older installs are moved off the retired 'production' channel name automatically.

Fixes ST-Link detection failing with 'the debug probe could not be created' - the Utility was holding its own connection to the ST-Link open while trying to connect a second time. Also renames the About page to Update / About.

Adds a searchable Help section covering every feature: player modes and twin stick, Disconnect/Keyboard mode and the DongleMaster, remapping, turbo, shortcuts, overlays and themes, kiosk mode, LaunchBox scripts, firmware updates, ST-Link flashing, update channels, backup, and troubleshooting. Type a word into the search box and matching topics open with the hits highlighted.

Corrects the ST-Link flashing guidance: when the chip can't be reached, the Utility now points at the usual causes - SWD wiring and making sure the board runs from its own power (an ST-Link's 3V3 pin can't power a whole board) - while it keeps retrying through a power-cycle.

The Test screen now shows the raw electrical state of every input pin - including the mode pins - straight off the connectors, perfect for checking cabinet wiring (needs this firmware). The keyboard test shows just the keys being sent right now instead of a wall of every mapped key, and both keyboard keys and mode-pin presses are announced by voice.

The Help section now says which boards each feature applies to (a 2000T has no 4-player mode, twin stick isn't available on the 3000T, the 4000H uses button combos instead of TURBO/8TO6 pins, and so on).

When your board already updates from the app, the ST-Link flashing tool is dimmed with a note pointing at the normal update button - it stays available for recovery.

Fixes in-app firmware updates failing with 'firmware package is inconsistent' - the app mis-read the update package header. Update the app first, then firmware updates install normally. (Found by installing firmware 20260708_0046 on the bench through the exact customer path.)

The Help section now covers Batocera, RetroPie and desktop Linux: what works today (keyboard mode out of the box, remote configuration from any browser or phone on your network), the one-time setup lines, and honest notes on gamepad support and on-screen overlays. Remote configuration stays open on your local network by default - viewing is always open, and an optional PIN can protect changes if you want it.

First PactoLink release for Linux emulation systems: Batocera, RetroPie, Lakka and desktop Linux.

Mode changes pop right on the cabinet screen (PC Batocera) or as RetroArch messages in-game, and the full Pacto configurator is served to any browser on your network at http://<cabinet-ip>:46810. Keyboard/Disconnect mode works out of the box for MAME-style play; native gamepad (XInput) support on Linux arrives with the upcoming "Linux mode" firmware update: switch the board's USB identity to Linux mode and Linux's own built-in Xbox-pad driver runs the controls directly.

One-line install on any of them: curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leecyrille/PactoTech_Public_Releases/main/install.sh | sh (RetroPie/desktop Linux: | sudo sh) - the script detects your system and installs the right signed package; the releases README has step-by-step instructions including how to open a terminal or SSH in. Batocera can also install with no terminal at all: drop the zip contents on the cabinet's share and launch "Install PactoLink" from the Ports menu. Raspberry Pi (aarch64) builds are included but still experimental. See the Help section in the app or web configurator for step-by-step guides.

Easier updates: the Update page now checks for updates automatically when opened, highlights the next step, and greys out anything that's already done; an "update available" notice appears in the sidebar next to the connection status. Fixed: the ST-Link section no longer stays highlighted after a successful flash.

Firmware fix: a "CONNECTING ARCADE CONTROLS - 12s" message could stay frozen on the overlay and SpecVision after power-on (on boards with a DongleMaster attached). This firmware fixes it, and the app's overlay now also clears a stuck message on older firmware by itself.

New - Windows / Linux mode (USB identity, Modes page): boards in Batocera, RetroPie or Lakka cabinets can be set to Linux mode, where the controls run on the system's own built-in Xbox 360 driver - real native gamepads, no extra software in the input path. The board keeps full configurator support via Keyboard mode on Windows, and the Help section covers everything including a one-line Linux installer.

Clearer settings: pinball inputs and mode-wiring options now always stay visible with per-board notes (greyed items explain which boards have them and how to add the feature with remapping), and the turbo switch wiring is spelled out (permanent ground on TURBO, switch on !TURB).
